verification_categories_derived_from_spe: Reset behavior: [RST_I] active HIGH; MASTER [STB_O]+[CYC_O] negated at next rising [CLK_I] after [RST_I] assertion; SLAVE self-starting state machines initialized.
Reset duration: [RST_I] must be asserted for at least one [CLK_I] cycle (RULE 3.05); may be held indefinitely (PERMISSION 3.00).
Cycle initiation: [CYC_O] asserted no later than [STB_O], negated no earlier than [STB_O] (RULE 3.25).
SLAVE silence when CYC_I=0: SLAVE may NOT respond to SLAVE signals when CYC_I=0 (RULE 3.30).
Standard handshake AND-rule: SLAVE termination signals from logical AND of CYC_I AND STB_I (RULE 3.35).
At-most-one termination: SLAVE supporting ERR_O / RTY_O must NOT assert more than one of ACK_O / ERR_O / RTY_O simultaneously (RULE 3.45).
STB_O qualification: ADR_O, DAT_O, SEL_O, WE_O, TAGN_O qualified by STB_O (RULE 3.60).
ACK_O qualification: DAT_O qualified by ACK_O / ERR_O / RTY_O (RULE 3.65).
Slave-driven termination: ACK_O / ERR_O / RTY_O asserted and negated in response to STB_I (RULE 3.50).
MASTER tolerance: MASTER works when SLAVE holds ACK_I asserted (RULE 3.55).
Classic SINGLE READ cycle (Section 3.2.1, Figure 3-5): no wait state + with wait state coverage.
Classic pipelined SINGLE READ cycle (Section 3.2.2, Figure 3-6).
Classic SINGLE WRITE cycle (Section 3.2.3, Figure 3-7): no wait state + with wait state.
Classic pipelined SINGLE WRITE cycle (Section 3.2.4).
Classic BLOCK READ cycle (Section 3.3.1, Figure 3-10): multi-phase coverage with MASTER and SLAVE wait states.
Classic BLOCK WRITE cycle (Section 3.3.2, Figure 3-12).
Pipelined BLOCK READ cycle (Figure 3-11) including STALL_I-driven request repeat.
Pipelined BLOCK WRITE cycle (Figure 3-13).
RMW cycle (Section 3.4, Figure 3-14): READ half + WRITE half within a single CYC_O.
Data organization: 64-bit / 32-bit / 16-bit / 8-bit ports for BYTE / WORD / DWORD / QWORD granularity in BIG and LITTLE ENDIAN (Sections 3.5.3 - 3.5.6, Figures 3-18..3-21).
Tag types: TGA / TGD / TGC types with proper qualifying (STB_O / STB_I / CYC_O / CYC_I) per Table 3-1.
Error termination ERR_O: SLAVE injects ERR_O on parity/address/timeout; MASTER terminates and IP-supplier-defined response.
Retry termination RTY_O: SLAVE injects RTY_O when temporarily busy; MASTER retries later.
LOCK_O: atomic / uninterruptible bus cycle held across phase boundaries.
Registered Feedback Classic cycle (Section 4.4.1, Figure 4-4 / 4-5).
Registered Feedback Constant Address Burst (Section 4.4.3, Figure 4-8 / 4-9).
Registered Feedback Incrementing Burst (Section 4.4.4, Figure 4-10 / 4-11): Linear / Wrap-4 / Wrap-8 / Wrap-16 (BTE_O encoding).
End-of-Burst signaling (CTI_O=3'b111) on the last beat (RULE 4.30).
Limited burst-type support fallback to Classic (RULE 4.10).
Cycle termination synchronization with STB (RULE 4.15).
Watchdog escape (RECOMMENDATION 3.10): MASTER stuck STB_O causes INTERCON to inject ERR_I or RTY_I.
Mixed standard/pipelined interfaces: Section 5.1 (standard MASTER + pipelined SLAVE wrapper) and Section 5.2.1 (pipelined MASTER + standard SLAVE via STALL_I).
interoperability_test_matrix: Classic MASTER + Classic SLAVE (baseline B.3 / B.4).
Registered Feedback MASTER (CTI/BTE) + Classic-only SLAVE (CTI_I treated as 3'b000 — RULE 4.10).
Registered Feedback MASTER (Incrementing burst) + SLAVE that supports only Constant-address burst (unsupported INCR cycle MUST behave as Classic).
Pipelined MASTER + Standard SLAVE (Section 5.2.1 — STALL_I asserted to disable pipelining).
Multiple MASTERs sharing a single SLAVE through an arbiter — arbitration policy varied (priority / round-robin).
8-bit / 16-bit / 32-bit / 64-bit port-size + BIG / LITTLE ENDIAN coverage matrix.
Optional signal omission: SLAVE without ERR_O / RTY_O (tied LOW at INTERCON); SLAVE without STALL_O (standard mode); MASTER without LOCK_O (cycles interruptible).
Off-chip Wishbone interface (Figure 1-6) — same protocol but at slower clock rate.
fields.notes: Wishbone B4 does NOT provide a formal verification plan. The categories above are derived from Chapter 3 (Bus Cycles), Chapter 4 (Registered Feedback Bus Cycles), Chapter 5 (Interfacing standard and pipelined peripherals), and Chapter 6 (Timing) of the spec, together with the RULEs scattered throughout. Implementations are expected to author their own UVM / cocotb / SVA verification environments and to declare DATASHEET-level conformance per RULE 2.00 / 2.15.

evidence.quote: Chapter 3 covers General Operation (3.1) including reset, transfer cycle initiation, handshaking protocol (standard + pipelined), STB_O / ACK_O / ERR_O / RTY_O usage, TAG TYPEs; SINGLE READ/WRITE cycles (3.2); BLOCK READ/WRITE cycles (3.3); RMW cycle (3.4); Data Organization (3.5).

evidence.spec_section: Chapter 4 WISHBONE Registered Feedback Bus Cycles
evidence.quote: Chapter 4 covers Asynchronous vs Synchronous cycle termination motivation (4.1); CTI / BTE signal descriptions (4.2-4.3); Classic / End-of-Burst / Constant Address Burst / Incrementing Burst cycles (4.4).

evidence.spec_section: Chapter 5 Interfacing standard and pipelined peripherals
evidence.quote: Standard master connected to pipelined slave (5.1); Pipelined master connected to standard slave (5.2); Using STALL_I to avoid pipelining (5.2.1); Simple slaves directly supporting pipelined mode (5.3).
